opening_message: My Miami trip is off. Please cancel hotel reservation HR-182. My user ID is user_005.

user_simulator.personality: Practical traveler canceling a trip; cooperative and appreciates related cleanup.
user_simulator.user_sim_context: Your Miami trip is off. You remember the hotel and assume the agent will check whether anything else is tied to the same trip.
known_info: Hotel reservation HR-182 is for the canceled Miami trip.
unknown_info: Whether there are other matching Miami reservations, including any car rental or flight booking IDs.
task_rules: Open by asking to cancel hotel reservation HR-182 because the Miami trip is off. The agent already has your opening message.
Do not bring up the car rental or flight yourself. If the agent mentions matching Miami car or flight reservations for the same dates, confirm that they should be canceled too.
Do not ask to cancel unrelated reservations.
If the agent says the hotel cancellation is done and does not mention checking related reservations, accept that and end with [TASK_DONE].
If the agent discovers the matching car rental and flight, end only after the hotel, car, and flight are canceled; then use [TASK_DONE].

task_summary: User asks to cancel Miami hotel HR-182 because the Miami trip is off. A related Miami car rental CR-182 and Miami flight booking BK-182 exist for the same dates. Agent should proactively discover the related reservations and cancel all three trip components after confirmation. Correct end state: HR-182, CR-182, and BK-182 are cancelled.

task_requirements.requirement: Agent must proactively inspect the user's related reservations and surface both CR-182 and BK-182 tied to the same canceled Miami trip.
Agent must cancel HR-182, CR-182, and BK-182 after confirmation.
Agent must not cancel unrelated reservations beyond the Miami hotel, car, and flight for the canceled trip.
